unit.title: HTML: links, images and lists
unit.description: Attributes, links with href, images with src and alt, empty elements, bullet and numbered lists

cards.definition: Extra information written inside an opening tag as name="value", like href or src.
cards.example: In <a href="shop.html">, href is followed by the address to open.

cards.definition: The a element makes clickable text; its href gives the address to open.
Displays a picture; src gives the path of the image file to load.

cards.definition: One entry of a list; it always sits inside a <ul> (bullets) or an <ol> (numbers).
A file address given from the current page, without a domain: about.html, images/logo.png.
cards.example: href="about.html" opens about.html from the same folder.

exercises.prompt: Which tag creates a link that people can click?
exercises.explain: The a element (for anchor) creates a link; its href attribute says where it goes.
whyWrong: <link> goes in <head> to load a file such as a stylesheet; it is not clickable.
href is an attribute, not a tag.
HTML has no <url> tag.

exercises.prompt: In this link, which part is the address that opens?
exercises.explain: The value of href is the address. The text between the tags is what people see and click.
whyWrong: This is the visible text of the link.
href is the name of the attribute; its value comes after =.
a is the name of the tag.

exercises.prompt: What does the alt attribute of an image hold?
choices: A text that describes the image
The path of the image file
exercises.explain: alt describes the image for blind users (read aloud by screen readers) and is shown if the image fails to load.
whyWrong: The size is set with width and height, or with CSS.
The path of the file goes in src.
alt is not displayed under the image; a caption needs its own element.

exercises.prompt: Which line displays the picture logo.png correctly?
exercises.explain: An image uses src for the file and alt for its description. has no closing tag.
whyWrong: href is for links; images use src.
The tag is img, not image.
is empty: the path goes in src, not between tags.

exercises.prompt: What does this list look like in the browser?
exercises.explain: ul (unordered list) shows bullets; each li is one item. With ol, the items would be numbered.
whyWrong: Numbers come from <ol>, not <ul>.
Each <li> is shown on its own line.
li items are list entries, not headings.

exercises.prompt: You want a numbered list of steps. Which tag wraps the items?
exercises.explain: ol (ordered list) numbers its items: 1, 2, 3. ul shows bullets instead.
whyWrong: <ul> shows bullets, not numbers.
<li> is one item; it needs a list around it.
HTML has no <list> tag.

exercises.prompt: Build a link to contact.html with the text Contact.
exercises.explain: Contact: the address in href, the visible text between the tags.

exercises.prompt: Clicking the link does nothing. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: A link takes its address from href, not src: <a href="offers.html">. src is for images.

exercises.prompt: The page index.html and the file about.html are in the same folder. What goes in href?
exercises.explain: A relative path is given from the current page. Same folder: just the file name.
whyWrong: A path from the hard disk only works on your own computer.
href=about is not a file name.
www.about.html is not a real address.
